STRUCTURES
IT CLAUSE
ADVERBIAL CLAUSE
1
It + Adverbial Clause
I hate it…

She loves it…

I don’t mind it...
When someone runs late all the time.

When the kids play quietly.

When someone laughs out loud.
2
It + Verb + Noun + Adverbial clause
It upsets me…

It bothers my dad...
When my mums shouts for no reason.

When my little brother is noisy.
There are some other phrases that may be considered adverbial clauses as well.

Condition:  if / Unless / As if / Only if - You’ll get permission only if your father agrees.
Place: Everywhere / Wherever / Anywhere - Wherever I go, I see her.
Reason: Now that / Because / Since - You can start painting the room now that your brother is gone.
Among the ways we can express perspectives, we can consider the following structures.

1. The other adverbial clauses are considered such since they can move within the sentences without affecting the meaning.

slideDifferences.publishedText: To Consider 1. The other adverbial clauses are considered such since they can move within the sentences without affecting the meaning. 2. There are also adverbial clauses of time, contrast, comparison: Time: Whenever you do that, I hate it! Contrast: Different from all we have seen, I still have one argument. Comparison: I am ok with all that as long as we all are safe.

slideDifferences.nativeText:
There are some functions that we can cover when using the grammar learned in this unit.
Functions
Examples
1
Express disagreement towards certain actions.
I hate it when someone yells in public.
It upsets my mum when we do not clean our room.
2
State enjoyment in regards certain actions.
It brightens my days when someone thinks on me and texts me.
I love it when my kids help me with the housework.
3
Show you are ok with people’s doings.
John did not bring white cardboard but yellow.
I don’t mind the color as long as he brought one.

slideDifferences.nativeText:
I really don’t mind it!

Keep it low, kids. I’m really sorry my friend.
Don’t worry, I really don’t mind it; in fact, up to certain level, kids need to be noisy.
I know, but sometimes I think mine overreact. 
I see. I have read that it stresses mums out when their children get too noisy and loud.
Totally! Don’t get me wrong, I love it when they seem happy but I am trying to teach them that there is no reason to be loud.
You know, it helps a lot when you keep them busy, so they drain energy in different activities.
Do you have any suggestions? Can you share them with me? Sorry to bother.
Sure, it doesn’t bother me at all.

I hate it…

She loves it…

I don’t mind it...

When someone runs late all the time.

When the kids play quietly.

When someone laughs out loud.
It + Verb + Noun + Adverbial clause

It upsets me…

It bothers my dad...

When my mums shouts for no reason.

When my little brother is noisy.

There are some other phrases that may be considered adverbial clauses as well.

Condition:  if / Unless / As if / Only if - You’ll get permission only if your father agrees.
Place: Everywhere / Wherever / Anywhere - Wherever I go, I see her.
Reason: Now that / Because / Since - You can start painting the room now that your brother is gone.
Among the ways we can express perspectives, we can consider the following structures.

There are some functions that we can cover when using the grammar learned in this unit.
Functions
Examples
Express disagreement towards certain actions.
I hate it when someone yells in public.
It upsets my mum when we do not clean our room.
State enjoyment in regards certain actions.
It brightens my days when someone thinks on me and texts me.
I love it when my kids help me with the housework.
Show you are ok with people’s doings.

John did not bring white cardboard but yellow.
I don’t mind the color as long as he brought one.
